why: Look down the third column: each figure loses one part. Row 1 has a circle, a curved hook and a dot; row 2 drops the circle and keeps the hook with its dot; so row 3 must drop the hook too and keep only the dot. That is option 3. Options 1 and 2 still have the circle, so they go backwards.
trick: When figures in a column get simpler step by step, the last one is usually the smallest part that is left.
note: The rule in this grid is not very clear; the "losing one part" rule down column 3 matches the book answer C.
